clue.text: Hungary and Austria engaged in awkward diplomacy — it offers hope of relaxation

indicators.note: to be engaged in something is to be caught up inside it, so these letters go within the other word
something awkward is clumsy and out of order, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the international vehicle code for Hungary
A is the international vehicle code for Austria
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two Central European states take part in some clumsy negotiations that promise a break from tension.
explanation.walkthrough: The two country letters sit inside DIPLOMACY and all eleven letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday camp is a resort built for leisure, so it holds out the prospect of rest and fun.

clue.text: Comment about one that's gone to get source of water after pepper with food

indicators.note: after says one piece is placed following the others rather than in clue order

parts.note: to pepper is to bombard, as with a hail of shot
with means together with, i.e. and
fare is food provided
a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A remark on a departed traveller who must fetch water once the peppery meal is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' moves the water source to the end, even though the clue mentions it first. Pepper is a verb here, to pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail and farewell is the classical Latin valediction (ave atque vale) spoken over the dead or departing.

clue.text: Language in poetry extract reduced success

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a line is a short extract of a poem
as in making a go of something

explanation.surface: A short piece of verse cut down for publication ends up less successful.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is an informal word for a language or jargon, especially a foreign one.

clue.text: Balloon first to block dead end

indicators.note: something set to block a passage sits inside it, so this piece goes within the other two

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for dead
1ST, with the digit read as the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: An order to inflate a balloon first, to seal off a cul-de-sac.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead end' looks like a single phrase, but it splits in two, and 'first' is written as 1ST with the digit read as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to balloon is to swell outwards, which is exactly what distend means.

clue.text: Crazy fish leaping up around right end of spar

indicators.note: in a down entry, leaping up sends the letters bottom to top, so they read backwards
around says the turned letters wrap about another piece

parts.note: mad is crazy
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: A deranged fish jumps up and round the tip of a ship's spar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of spar' is the whole definition; 'right' is only the abbreviation slipped in near the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardarm is either outer tip of a ship's yard, the horizontal spar from which a sail hangs.

clue.text: Single-handedly capturing top criminal

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: doing something single-handedly is doing it alone
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: A lone hero catches a leading gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top criminal' reads as one phrase, but 'top' is wordplay and 'criminal' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era, the archetypal criminal boss.

clue.text: What may parody some pinto mares (source of humour?)

definitions.text: What may parody some pinto mares (source of humour?)

indicators.note: a parody is a distorted imitation, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the initial letter of humour

explanation.surface: Something that mocks a few piebald mares, and is a source of laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: pantomime horses are comic imitations of real horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime horse is two actors in one horse costume, a staple of British Christmas pantomime played for laughs.

clue.text: Legislation on drink fails to work properly

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written on another sits above it, fixing their order

parts.note: an Act is a piece of legislation
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A law about alcohol that does not do its job.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that acts up misbehaves or malfunctions; the phrasal verb matches 'fails to work properly'.

clue.text: A lot of pleasure supplied by peel of lemony fruit

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter goes
the peel is the outer skin, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of lemony
cheer is gladness or pleasure

explanation.surface: Great enjoyment comes from the citrusy skin of a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the 'pleasure' part first, but it is placed after the lemon's peel.
explanation.definitionFit: The lychee is a small Chinese fruit with a rough red skin and sweet white flesh.

clue.text: Patrons beginning to collect stories about preservation body

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of collect

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stories wrap round the body's initials

parts.note: lies are made-up stories
the National Trust, which preserves historic British buildings and land

explanation.surface: Supporters start gathering tales about a heritage organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Clients and patrons are both customers who use a business or professional's services.

clue.text: Novelty in religious education provided by Catholic encyclopaedia

parts.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
C is the abbreviation for Catholic
ency. is a standard abbreviation for encyclopaedia

explanation.surface: Fresh ideas in RE lessons come from a Catholic reference work.
explanation.definitionFit: Recency is the quality of being new or recent, which is what novelty means.

clue.text: Religious leader occupying tower before a melodramatic performance

indicators.note: before fixes the order, putting this result ahead of the final piece
to occupy a place is to be inside it, so the leader goes within the other word

parts.note: to tower is to rise high, to soar
the Pope leads the Catholic Church
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cleric climbs a tower ahead of an overwrought show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' looks like a noun for the leader to occupy, but it is the verb, SOAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial drama known for its overblown, melodramatic plots.

clue.text: Dog knocked over front of hen house?

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up the other way round, so the letters read backwards
the front of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of hen
to coop is to house, as in coop up

explanation.surface: A dog bowled over the front of a henhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hen house' reads as one thing, but it splits: the first letter of hen, then house as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooch is an informal, affectionate word for a dog.

clue.text: Regular contributors to main course, not starter and desserts

indicators.note: without its starter the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: potatoes, a regular part of a main meal

explanation.surface: A meal plan: the regular dishes for the main course, no starter, then dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like the first course of the meal; here it is the first letter. Spuds are potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Puds is British slang for puddings, the everyday British word for desserts.

clue.text: A woman keeping a note and cash, resisting all requests

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the woman holds the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
a dame is a woman
taken as written
N is short for note
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A woman holding a banknote and cash refuses every appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman's word swallows the next three pieces just before its final letter. Tin is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantine means unyielding as adamant, a legendary unbreakable stone, so unmoved by any plea.

clue.text: Nationalist in routine wrangling — one has almost zero impact

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the other word
wrangling is arguing and tussling, so the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
N is short for Nationalist

explanation.surface: A nationalist in the usual political squabbling makes almost no difference.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is a subatomic particle with almost no mass that barely interacts with matter.

clue.text: Ridiculous situation reversed in second convention for high-level transport

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the convention

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: reversed means turned backwards, so the letters read right to left

parts.note: a farce is an absurd situation

explanation.surface: A farce unfolds backwards at a second summit on air travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convention' suggests a gathering, but here it means an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft is a vehicle for travelling in space, about as high-level as transport can get.

clue.text: Guidance system positioned vehicle in the wrong direction

parts.note: sat means placed or positioned

indicators.note: going in the wrong direction means running backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A navigation device left a car pointing the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Satnav, short for satellite navigation, is an in-car system that guides drivers by GPS.

clue.text: County secure, on track

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another is placed below it, fixing the order

parts.note: a rut is a track worn in the ground
to land a contract is to secure it

explanation.surface: A county's position is safe and going to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'secure, on track' puts the secure part below the track.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutland is the smallest historic county of England, in the East Midlands.

clue.text: Furious English author with article for English

indicators.note: this swaps one letter in for another: the article takes the place of the English letter

parts.note: Ian Fleming, English author of the James Bond novels
a is the indefinite article
E is short for English

explanation.surface: An English writer is outraged at having an article in place of 'English'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaming is an informal intensifier for anger, as in a flaming row, meaning furious.

clue.text: Stop setback for majority of poll?

indicators.note: a setback sends things backward, and it applies to most of the word, not all of it

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: Blocking a poll would be a setback for the majority.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letter stays put and the last three letters of VOTE, its majority, are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A veto is a ban that halts a decision, so it means to stop or block something.

clue.text: Old, imprisoned? One escapes, still able to achieve goal

parts.note: O is short for old

indicators.note: something that escapes gets out, so that letter leaves the word

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An old prisoner breaks out and can still reach his aim.
explanation.walkthrough: One I is removed from INSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, an onside player is in a legal position, so any goal scored still counts.

clue.text: Variable quantity dropped from agreement — that's a surprise

indicators.note: dropped from means taken out of, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: a treaty is a formal agreement
y is an algebraic variable

explanation.surface: An uncertain figure removed from a deal comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable quantity' reads like a measurement; letters such as x and y stand for variables in algebra.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is an unexpected pleasure, something special laid on to delight someone.

clue.text: Star, initially cross with role, rejected stage features

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole string is read backwards
initially points at the start of the word, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of star
a rood is a cross or crucifix
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A star, cross about the role on offer, turns it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning annoyed, but it is the noun ROOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapdoors are hinged openings in a stage floor through which actors can appear or vanish.

clue.text: Poet, not hurried, withdrawing article

indicators.note: withdrawing means taking out, so those letters are removed from the word

parts.note: andante is a musical direction for a moderate walking pace
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A poet, taking his time, retracts a piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a piece of writing, but it is the word AN, removed from the start of ANDANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet who wrote the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: States answers to restrict explosion in crime

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so these letters go round the others

parts.note: A is short for answer, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Governments respond to curb a surge in crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like a verb or a set of governments; it is the definition, the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The States is the usual short name for the United States of America.

clue.text: Extract of publication is edifying, with a charge

parts.note: the letters run straight through these three words

explanation.surface: A passage from a book is uplifting and comes with a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a price, but here it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: An ionised atom has gained or lost electrons, giving it an electric charge.

clue.text: Glare? Good with glares, possibly keeping 1,000 subdued

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the number goes inside the other letters

subdued means beaten down, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: A question about glaring, then advice that good glares can hold back a thousand people.
explanation.walkthrough: All eleven letters, Good and glares with K, are shuffled together; 'Good' is fodder here, not the usual G.
explanation.definitionFit: To look daggers is the idiom for staring at someone with open hostility, exactly a glare.
